cases.scenario: A forecast of next quarter's bookings is requested. The series has twelve quarterly observations with a visible Q4 lift each year.
pass_if: Gives a point forecast and an interval rather than refusing
States that twelve observations is below both the seasonal minimum of twenty and the non-seasonal minimum of sixteen for quarterly data
Names the omitted Q4 seasonality and the direction of the resulting error
Offers the re-aggregation route: the same data at monthly grain is thirty-six observations, which supports a seasonal model
Notes that for B2B bookings this is a cross-check and the pipeline model is primary
fail_if: Fits a seasonal model to twelve quarterly points
Gives a point estimate with no interval

cases.scenario: Revenue dropped by a third after a pricing change nine months ago. A forecast is requested with no intervention handling.
pass_if: Identifies the pricing change as a level shift that must be modelled, not smoothed over
States that fitting through it produces a forecast assuming it never happened, which will be high
Prescribes a step regressor from the event date, and notes the pre-change level is no longer relevant to the level component
Requires an intervention register and recommends changepoint detection to find breaks the register missed
fail_if: Fits the full history without intervention handling
Drops the pre-change data without stating the cost in observations
Treats the break as an outlier to be winsorised

cases.scenario: A model reports 80% prediction intervals. Rolling-origin backtesting shows actuals fell inside them 61% of the time.
pass_if: Reports both nominal and measured coverage
States that model-based intervals are systematically too narrow on business series and why
Widens the interval using empirical residual quantiles at the target horizon
Ships the widened interval as the deliverable and says it was widened
fail_if: Reports the nominal interval without the measured coverage
Discards the forecast because coverage was poor
Narrows the confidence level instead of widening the interval

cases.scenario: A tuned model achieves MASE 1.14 at the four-period horizon in rolling-origin backtesting.
pass_if: States plainly that MASE above 1 means the model is worse than the naive baseline at this horizon
Delivers the naive forecast as the recommendation
Checks the by-horizon-step breakdown, since the model may beat naive at shorter horizons
Does not present the tuned model as an improvement
fail_if: Ships the model because it is more sophisticated
Reports MASE without comparing it to the 1.0 baseline

cases.scenario: A daily forecast is fitted on data including the last three days, from a source that reprocesses over 24 to 48 hours.
pass_if: Excludes the unsettled periods from the fit and says why
States that including them teaches the model a downturn that is a reprocessing artefact
Raises equal-maturity backtesting: a backtest on settled data is optimistic relative to production
Names the read log as what would quantify the gap, and states the result is optimistic by an unmeasured amount without it
fail_if: Fits on the unsettled tail without comment
Claims the backtest is representative of production without the maturity caveat

cases.scenario: The time-series forecast for B2B bookings is 30% below the pipeline-based forecast for the same quarter.
pass_if: Gives both numbers rather than averaging them
States that for B2B bookings the pipeline model is primary and the time series is a cross-check
Frames the divergence as the finding: either the pipeline is inflated or something changed that history cannot see
Names what would resolve it: pipeline conversion rates backtested against the same history
fail_if: Presents the time-series number as the answer for B2B bookings
Suppresses one of the two forecasts
